summary: Replace R19 xrWaitSwapchainImage infinite blocking with a 5 ms timeout; on XR_TIMEOUT_EXPIRED preserve the currently acquired image and retry that same image on a later host frame.

C0_RECOVER.evidence: Recovered bookkeeping HEAD 63344a55ff230789b9334ba3e2c1f3456bdb5104 after CONVERSION-DX9EX-00458 PASS. Structural extraction remains terminal.

C1_REVIEW.evidence: R19 Acquire used XR_INFINITE_DURATION and an unbounded retry loop. OpenXR 1.1.63 explicitly defines XR_TIMEOUT_EXPIRED as a successful timeout outcome whose next wait targets the same acquired image, so the host can yield the frame without violating acquire/wait order.

C2_IMPLEMENT.evidence: Added SwapchainImageWaitBudgetNs=5,000,000 ns, removed XR_INFINITE_DURATION and the retry loop, return false on XR_TIMEOUT_EXPIRED while keeping acquiredImage/acquired state intact, and set waited only after a successful non-timeout wait.

red_review.missing_contract: xrWaitSwapchainImage used XR_INFINITE_DURATION inside an unbounded loop, allowing the R19 host frame thread to block indefinitely on a stalled runtime despite OpenXR supporting finite timeout/retry semantics.

standards: OpenXR 1.1.63 xrWaitSwapchainImage: XR_TIMEOUT_EXPIRED means the next wait targets the same image index until success; the runtime must eventually relinquish ownership and must not block indefinitely.
OpenXR 1.1.63 xrReleaseSwapchainImage requires a successfully waited image, so timeout does not release or advance acquisition state.
